tasks.commitBody: The layer every rights rule stands on can now be cited: the bucket mechanism — three property objects materialized at write time, a read returning exactly one of them by tier priority — carries identifiers of its own, closing the gap where ER-1 and ER-3 presupposed a foundation nobody could point at and the document's own working-notes rule was unfollowable on its own base. The scheme gains one sentence: a Stands on: line names the rules a rule cannot be stated without, the foundation counterpart to Qualifications' bounding, and ER-1 and ER-3 now carry it instead of leaning silently. The sweep the issue commissioned — if a rule cannot be stated without relying on something, that something is a rule — surfaced the layers the war-story-driven inventory never reached, because the foundational layer is the one nobody gets wrong and so nobody writes down; what it found is now identified with its evidence, and what its evidence could not support is reported rather than smoothed over. ER-7, which already cited the foundation and cited it by section number — the one form of reference this scheme exists to abolish — now cites the identifiers instead, the worked example of the sweep found in the wild by the PO while verifying an unrelated citation. The foundation's identifiers are the next free numbers, not low ones: a base layer numbered after seventeen findings reads like a filing error, and the temptation to renumber or slot an ER-0 in front is exactly the silent-repointing failure the opaque creation-order scheme prevents. Section prose is byte-identical throughout: this commit gives the foundation addresses, and changes nothing it says. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills>.
